en: The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is a critically endangered species endemic to the country's tropical rainforests.
The Sampaguita, the national flower, is a fragrant white jasmine scientifically known as Jasminum sambac.
The Philippines declared independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
The Legislative branch of the Philippine government, which makes laws, is composed of the Senate and the House of Representatives.
Jose Rizal, the Philippine national hero, was a polymath who excelled in ophthalmology, literature, and the sciences.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces using ancient, sustainable irrigation engineering carved into the Cordillera mountains.
During the Lucban Pahiyas Festival, locals decorate their houses with kiping, which are colorful, leaf-shaped rice wafers.
Filipino, the national language, is primarily based on Tagalog and is written using the modern 28-letter alphabet.
Dr. Fe del Mundo, a pioneering Filipino pediatrician, invented a makeshift incubator using native bamboo baskets.
The traditional Filipino value of bayanihan is historically demonstrated by neighbors physically carrying a nipa hut to a new location.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, is one of the world's smallest primates with enormous eyes for night vision.
Under the Philippine Constitution, citizens who are at least eighteen years old have the right and duty to vote.
